Campus Chaos - UP and UFS

By: Este de Klerk | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What's behind explosive protests erupting at the University of the Free State, TUKS and other SA campuses?

Summary:
What has fuelled ongoing violence on South African University Campuses this year? As students continue to protest against outsourcing of critical university services, the issue of Afrikaans as a medium of instruction and racial tensions have added to the simmering tensions on campuses as this week's protests and clashes at UP and UFS have made apparent

Further information:
TUKS
Tension that flared at the end of last week, resumed on the Hadfield and Groenkloof campuses of the University of Pretoria on Monday over the use of Afrikaans as a medium of instruction. Scuffles first broke out between AfriForum Youth and Economic Freedom Fighters Student Command (EFFSC) members on Thursday during a consultative meeting over languages at the institution. The situation deteriorated into a clash between black students and their Afrikaner counterparts. White students stood their ground and declared they would no longer watch and do nothing while their language was being attacked.The protesters, under the #AfrikaansMustFall banner, are demanding the total removal of Afrikaans as a medium of instruction at the university. The campaign was initiated by the EFF student command last week.Demonstrations to have Afrikaans removed as a language of instruction have been plaguing the institution since last week, This moved management last week to obtain an interdict against unlawful protesting.Economic Freedom Fighters student command (EFFSC) nevertheless organised new protests on Monday, with its main rival AfriForum Youth seeking to protect students’ right to study. The university announced on Monday that it would submit proposals for English to become the sole language of instruction at the university. Processes to this end were underway, it said. 24 students appeared in court on charges of public violence
UNIVERSITY OF THE FREE STATE
Then, on Monday UFS suspended lectures after violence erupted at the Varsity cup between rugby supporters and protesters. An SMS sent to students read: “UFS Bfn Campus closed 23-24 Feb 2016 due to strike and protest. Safety of staff and students our priority.” Students had apparently gone on the rampage and vandalised two men’s hostels. Unconfirmed allegations from insiders were that white students were being assaulted on campus. A video, reportedly taken on campus on Monday afternoon, showed rugby players and supporters assaulting a group of protesters who had gone on to the field, disrupting the FNB Varsity Cup rugby match between the UFS Shimlas and the Madibaz. Workers were protesting today demanding the implementation of last year’s agreement to end outsourcing and demanding the reinstatement of Trevor Shaku, a leader of #OutsourcingMustFall and the Socialist Youth Movement, who was dismissed from his post as a research assistant at the university for his role in the campaign, said students. The students alleged that the UFS management, colluding with the police, were trying to dismantle the campaign and intimidate workers and students. It was alleged that 34 students had been arrested following disruptions at the university. The protesting students have called on white students to support them in their cause. “One of the best features of the #FeesMustFall movement was the unity of black and white. Struggle and solidarity overcame racial divisions. “We call on white students to mobilise alongside their black brothers and sisters to protest against reactionary attempts to divert this class struggle into a racial conflict,” the students said. The University of Free State did not immediately provide further details on the situation.

Press Release:


Campus Chaos
From protests over outsourcing of critical services, to eradication of Afrikaans as a medium of instruction, the cost of fees and racial tension, university campuses countrywide have this year played host to scenes of chaos. What is behind yet more violence and vandalism at the Universities of Pretoria, the Free State and North West this week, and to what extent have fringe elements hijacked legitimate student causes for political gain? Carte Blanche reports.
